newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil keeps mum on CVRD sell-off details.
newsitem.headline: Brazil keeps mum on CVRD sell-off details.

text.p: Brazil on Wednesday dashed market hopes it would set an asking price for shares to be sold in the upcoming privatisation of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), but produced what it said was an answer to critcism of the sale.

Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said the asking price for the block sale of 40 percent to 45 percent of the mining giant's voting shares would be announced one day before the publication of tender details relating to that sale.

National Development Bank (BNDES) privatisation director Jose Pio Borges told reporters the tender details would be published at the end of February or early in March and the block sale would "probably" take place 45 days after that.
Shares in CVRD fell 1.54 percent after surging on speculation the government would finalise details of what is set to become South America's biggest privatisation.
The government hopes to raise more than $5 billion by privatising its 51 percent stake in CVRD, first through the block sale and then via sales to staff and sales on international stock markets.

Kandir and Borges said they had found an answer to critics who accused the government of selling off untold mineral wealth lying undetected in two neighbouring areas of the Amazonian state of Para which are controlled by CVRD.
Opponents of the privatisation have seized on reports of massive but undefined gold, copper and other mineral deposits in Carajas and Serra do Leste to demand the sale be stopped.
